transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um, I'm hoping I'm in the right place, and I don't want to take up too much of your time if it's nothing. 

I guess I came in because... well, for a long time now, I've just had this sort of heavy, low feeling sitting on me most days. I mean, I'm still getting through all my driving routes just fine, and I'm keeping up with my volunteer shifts, so I'm doing okay, really. It's not like I'm falling apart or anything. I just... I feel like I'm mostly just going through the motions, you know? Instead of really being in my own life. 

I hope I'm explaining that right. Is that the kind of thing I should be coming here for?
How long have you been experiencing this heavy, low feeling?

Well, let's see... it's been a while, honestly. I'd say about three years? It, um, it sort of started right around the time my dad passed away. 

I mean, I know everybody loses their parents eventually, and I really shouldn't be complaining because people deal with way worse stuff every day. I'm probably just making too big a deal out of it, to be honest. But yeah, it's been about three years since he died. 

I hope it's okay that I'm bringing that up... does that sound like a normal amount of time to still be feeling this way?
Do you find yourself enjoying the things you used to enjoy, like your volunteer work, as much as you did before your dad passed away?

Well, I... I guess I still enjoy it somewhat. I mean, the people at the food bank are really great, and I know it's important work. I don't want to sound ungrateful or like I don't care, because I really do. 

But, um... maybe I don't get quite the same spark out of it that I used to? Like, I still go, and I smile and do my part, but inside it just feels a little more like... like work, I suppose. Not that it's a burden! I just don't feel that same lift I used to get when I'd finish a shift. 

Is that terrible to say? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad person, admitting that. I'm still doing it all, I promise.
Are there any activities or things that you still enjoy and look forward to?

Um, well... I mean, I still like watching the football games on Sundays. I always make sure to catch those. And I like keeping my truck clean, you know? It's nice when it's all washed and looks good for the route. 

But I guess... I don't know if I really *look forward* to them the way I used to? I just sort of do them because that's what I've always done. It's not like I'm miserable doing them or anything! I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping all weekend. I'm still keeping busy. 

I just... I guess I don't really get excited about much of anything lately. Is that... is that okay to admit? I feel like I should be more positive about things.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight over the past three years?

Um, my weight? Well... no, not really. I mean, I think it's stayed pretty much the same. 

I try to keep an eye on it, you know? Being in the truck all day, it's easy to just grab fast food, but I try not to let myself go. I don't want to be one of those guys who just gives up on taking care of himself. So, I think my clothes all still fit about the same as they did back then. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, it's good that my weight is stable, right? I'm trying to do at least that part right.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns over the past three years?

Well, um... I guess my sleep is mostly fine. I always make sure I'm up and ready for work, I promise you that. I'm never late. 

But... I suppose on nights before a run, I tend to just lie there for a while? Just thinking about the next day's stops and making sure I have everything straight in my head. And sometimes I'll wake up around four in the morning and I can't really get back to sleep after that. So, even when I make it to work right on time, I kind of feel like I'm starting the day already worn down. 

I try really hard not to let it affect my job, though! I push right through it. Is that... do you think that's just a normal part of getting a little older? Waking up early like that? I hope it doesn't mean I'm doing something wrong with my routine.
Have you ever thought about ending your life?

Oh! No, no, absolutely not. I would never do something like that. 

I mean, sure, I get a little down sometimes, like I said, but... I would never actually think about hurting myself or ending things. I have too much respect for my job and... and the people I work with to just leave them hanging like that. I know I have responsibilities, and I always make sure to follow through on them. 

I hope you don't think I'm that bad off? I'm really trying my best to keep everything together and keep moving forward. That's the right way to handle things, isn't it? Just keeping your chin up and doing your work?
Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened in your life?

Guilty? Um... no, not really. I mean, I try to just do my best and be a good person, you know? 

I guess sometimes I feel bad if I'm running late on a delivery or if I make a mistake at work, but I always apologize and try to fix it right away. I don't want anyone to think I'm not reliable or that I don't care about my job. I really do care. 

But as for like, deep guilt about my life... no, I don't think so. I've always tried to do the right thing and be responsible. That's what you're supposed to do, right? Just do your best and try not to let people down? I hope I'm doing that okay.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now feel completely uninterested in?

Um... activities I used to enjoy? Well, no, not really. I mean, I still like the things I've always liked. 

I guess I don't go out and do as much on the weekends as I used to, but... that's just because I'm usually pretty tired from driving all week, you know? It's not that I don't *want* to do things, I just... I need to make sure I'm rested up so I can be sharp for work on Monday. I don't want to overdo it and end up making a mistake on the road. 

I still enjoy watching the game on Sunday afternoons, though! I always make time for that. It's important to have a little downtime, right? Just to recharge the batteries? I think it's pretty normal for a guy my age to slow down a little bit on the weekends, don't you?
Are there things that you used to find pleasurable but no longer do?

Oh, um... I guess that's sort of like what we were just talking about, right? With the activities? But, yeah, no... I can't really think of anything else. I still get a kick out of the same stuff I always have. 

A hot cup of coffee before my route, catching the sports radio while I'm on the road... I still really like all of that. I'm a pretty simple guy, you know? It doesn't take a whole lot for me. I just try to appreciate the little things so I can keep a good attitude for my deliveries and the customers. That's a good way to look at it, don't you think? Just trying to stay positive and appreciate what you have?
Are there things that used to bring you a lot of joy, but now you don't find enjoyable at all?

Um... boy, I feel like I'm giving you the same answer again, I'm sorry. But... no, I really can't think of anything like that. 

I mean, joy is a strong word, I guess. I don't know if I've ever been the type to jump up and down about things, but I definitely still enjoy my life. I still like my routine. I like getting my truck loaded up in the morning and hitting the road. 

I'm really trying to be helpful here, I promise. I just... I don't want you to think I'm holding anything back, because I'm not. I'm just a regular guy who goes to work and comes home. I hope that's okay? I mean, it's normal to just be content with a quiet life, right?
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to find pleasurable since your father passed away?

Oh... since my dad passed? Um... well, no, I wouldn't say so. I mean, losing him was... it was really tough, obviously. But I didn't stop liking things because of it. 

If anything, I try to keep up with the stuff we used to talk about, like the Sunday games, just to... I don't know, keep his memory going, I guess. I hope I'm not frustrating you by saying no to this kind of question again. I really am trying to give you what you need, I promise. It's just... I've always tried to keep a brave face and keep moving forward. That's what he would have wanted for me, anyway. That's the right way to handle things, isn't it? Just keeping on with your routine and doing your best?
Have you felt less interested in social activities since your father passed away?

Oh, social activities? Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I'm pretty much the same as I always was. I still talk to the guys at the depot in the mornings, and I'll chat with the customers on my route. 

I've never been a huge party guy or anything, so it's not like I'm suddenly staying home all the time when I used to be out every night. I just... I like my quiet time after a long shift. I hope that makes sense? I mean, it's pretty normal for a guy my age to just want to relax after driving all day, right? I'm really trying to make sure I'm answering these right for you. I haven't really pulled away from anyone, I just stick to my regular routine. That's okay, isn't it?
Do you feel like your low mood is interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Um... well, no, not really interfering, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm still showing up for my shifts every day, and I still go to help out at the food pantry on the weekends. I would never let people down like that. 

I guess... well, I suppose things take a little more pushing than they used to? Like, it takes a bit more effort to get myself out the door. But I still do it. I did... um, I did leave an application for a logistics supervisor position sitting on my desk unfinished. I just... I don't know, I guess I worried I wouldn't be able to keep up with the extra responsibilities right now, and I didn't want to make a bad impression on the higher-ups. 

But as far as my regular day-to-day, I'm still getting it all done. That's the important thing, right? As long as I'm still doing my job and handling my responsibilities, a little extra effort is just... well, it's just part of getting older, isn't it? I hope I'm explaining that okay. I really don't want you to think I'm slacking off or anything.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in the number of activities you enjoy doing since your father passed away?

Um... well, no, I wouldn't say there's been a significant decrease. I mean, I still have the things I like to do. I still watch the games, and I still like tinkering with my truck when I have the time. 

I guess... maybe I don't do quite as much as I did years ago, but that's just because I'm busy, you know? Between the routes and trying to keep the house in order, there's just not as much time for hobbies. But I haven't dropped everything. I still try to stay active when I can. 

I hope it doesn't seem like I'm just saying no to everything you ask. I really am trying to give you the right answers. It's just... I'm a pretty simple guy, and I've never had a ton of hobbies to begin with. So it's not like I've stopped doing a bunch of things I used to love. That's pretty normal, right? Just keeping things simple?
Have you had a period of at least two weeks in the past three years where you felt completely back to your normal self, without any of the low mood or loss of interest in activities?

Um... completely back to normal? Well... I guess I'd have to say I'm not really sure. I mean, I can't really pinpoint a specific couple of weeks where I felt, like, perfectly energetic and had zero worries, if that's what you mean. 

But I wouldn't say I've been doing terrible, either! It's just been sort of... a steady middle ground, I guess? Just waking up, doing my routes, and getting the job done. It's just normal life. I figure nobody feels a hundred percent perfect every single day, right? Especially at my age, you just kind of get used to a certain baseline. 

I hope that answers what you're looking for? I'm really trying to give you the right information here, I just don't think I've kept track of time quite like that. Am I making sense?
Have you had any period, no matter how short, where you felt completely back to your normal self since your father passed away?

Um... completely back to my normal self? Well... no, I guess I wouldn't say there's been any specific time like that. Not completely. 

But I mean, I'm doing okay! It's not like I'm falling apart or anything. It's just... well, since he passed, things have just been a little quieter, I guess you could say. Just a little more steady. I still have good days where I get my deliveries done early and things go smooth. It's just that the baseline is maybe a little... flatter? 

I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping all the time, though. I'm really not. I'm keeping up with everything. It's just hard to say I've felt a hundred percent like the old me, but that's just part of grieving and getting older, right? I hope that's the kind of answer you need... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Have you had any period of at least two weeks where you felt nearly constant sadness or a lack of interest in most things?

Um... constant sadness? For two weeks straight? No, definitely not. I mean, I really don't think so. 

Like I said, things have been a bit flatter, maybe a little quieter, but I haven't been just... down in the dumps non-stop. I still get up, I still do my routes, I still talk to the guys at the depot. If I was sad all the time, I don't think I'd be able to keep up with my job, right? 

And as for not being interested in things... well, I still care about getting my work done right, and keeping the truck running. I'm not just staring at the wall or anything like that. I really try to keep a positive attitude, all things considered. I hope that makes sense? I'm just trying to be as accurate as I can for you. I wouldn't want you to think I'm doing worse than I actually am.
Have you felt a persistent low mood for most of the past three years?

Um... a persistent low mood? Well... I really don't want to make it sound like I'm just miserable all the time, because I'm definitely not. I mean, I actually came in to see you because... well, for a long time now, I've been getting through my routes just fine, and keeping up with my volunteer shifts and everything. But... I guess there is this sort of heavy, low feeling that just kind of sits on me most days. 

It's almost like I'm just going through the motions, rather than really being in my own life, if that makes sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm complaining too much. Like I said, I'm still doing what I need to do and taking care of business! Does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you.
Has your low mood come and gone over the past three years, or has it been pretty much constant?

Um... come and gone? Well, I guess... it's been pretty constant, honestly. I don't want to make it sound like I've just been dragging my feet every single day for three years, because I really do try to keep my chin up. 

But... yeah, that quiet, heavy feeling... it doesn't really go away. It's just sort of always there in the background, even when I'm having a decent day on the road. It's not like a rollercoaster or anything, just... a steady sort of flat. 

I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I mean, I'm still functioning fine, you know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea. Is that the kind of detail you were looking for?
